subject: Coordination: POC hands-on + throughput dry-run windows
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Park <janelle@tegralabs.com>, ops-team@tegralabs.com
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Coordination: POC hands-on + throughput dry-run windows

Hi Janelle / Tegralabs ops team —

Quick note to align calendars for the hands-on POC kickoff and a separate throughput dry-run. Goal is to run a working session for prompt review and routing decisions, then a follow-up load window to validate throughput targets and latency SLOs against your production-like prompt mix.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Week 1: 2-hour hands-on kickoff (prompt review, routing matrix, canary routing plan)
- Week 2: 3-hour throughput dry-run (test harness walkthrough + steady-state load + spike tests)

Availability windows (PST):
- Tue 2027-06-15: 10:00–12:00 or 14:00–16:00
- Wed 2027-06-16: 09:00–11:00 or 15:00–18:00
- Thu 2027-06-17: 13:00–16:00

A few asks so we can size the dry-run:
- Desired steady-state throughput target (reqs/s) and 95th/99th latency SLOs you want us to validate
- Target prompt mix (short/med/long), and whether KV-cache behavior should match your prod (we can disable to stress test)
- Any IP/fixture data sets or rate limits we should be aware of

Attached: redwood_poc_runbook_v0.3.pdf (draft agenda + entry criteria) and test_harness_readme.md.

If any of the proposed windows work, I’ll send calendar invites and a preliminary canary run plan. CC’d Dylan and Rishi to confirm infra requirements.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Janelle Park <janelle@tegralabs.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, ops-team@tegralabs.com
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: POC hands-on + throughput dry-run windows

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the clear plan. We’re excited to run this with you. Quick answers below and a couple of constraints from our side: 

Availability: Wed 2027-06-16 afternoon (15:00–17:30) looks best for the hands-on kickoff. For the throughput dry-run, Thu 2027-06-24 09:00–12:30 PDT would be preferable.

Throughput/latency targets (what we’re aiming to validate):
- Steady-state target: 350 req/s for average prompt mix
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms, 99th <= 450ms (p95/p99 measured at token immediate response)

Prompt mix: roughly 55% short (<=128 tokens), 35% medium (129–512), 10% long (512–2048). We can provide a sample set (10k prompts) if you want to preload the harness.

We also prefer the dry-run to emulate prod KV-cache enabled, but we can run a second spike test with cache disabled if you recommend it.

Small ask: can you move the kickoff window to Wed afternoon rather than morning? We have multiple product folks who are remote in APAC and that slot avoids overlaps.

I’ll loop in our procurement contact if we need to finalize scheduling logistics.

—Janelle
Janelle Park
Head of ML Ops, Tegralabs
janelle@tegralabs.com

Date: 2027-06-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Coordination: POC hands-on + throughput dry-run windows

Hey all —

Thanks for the heads-up. We can support the Wed 2027-06-16 15:00–17:30 kickoff and Thu 2027-06-24 09:00–12:30 dry-run. A few infra notes so the dry-run is useful: 

- Recommended reserved capacity for dry-run: 4 x A100-style GPUs (or equivalent) with 48GB each to simulate tail latencies.
- Test harness: I’ve added a pre-dry-run smoke script in Drive (see link below) that runs 100 warmup requests across the three prompt lengths. Please run that 48 hours prior to the window.
- Cache plan: Janelle — since you prefer KV-cache enabled in prod, we’ll run the steady-state with cache on, then a 20-min spike test with cache disabled to observe cold-start behavior.
- Measurement: we’ll capture token-level traces and E2E latency (ingest -> token-return). Bring your p95/p99 target metrics so we can annotate them in the dashboard.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPOC-Runbook (runbook + smoke script)

I’ll coordinate with infra to reserve the machines and flag any maintenance windows. Rishi — can you confirm model variant/quantization profile we should use for benchmarks?

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Great — thanks everyone for the quick replies.

Confirmed schedule: 
- Hands-on POC kickoff (prompt review + routing): Wed 2027-06-16, 15:00–17:30 PDT
- Throughput dry-run (test harness + steady-state + spikes): Thu 2027-06-24, 09:00–12:30 PDT

Action items: 
- Tegralabs: share the 10k sample prompt set and any rate-limit constraints (by EOD 2027-06-14).
- Dylan: run the smoke script 48 hours prior and reserve infra (4 x A100 equiv).
- Rishi: recommend model variant/quant profile for the dry-run and send config by 2027-06-18.
- Monica: I’ll send calendar invites and attach the final runbook (v0.4) once Rishi’s profile is set.

I uploaded an updated runbook to Drive (same folder) and attached the v0.3 PDF for your review. If anything changes on timing, flag it here and I’ll re-run scheduling.

Thanks — looking forward to running this.

Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
